title: ASCII Kinesis V2 Strikes015 — Distal Mass Reversal Lag Debt

principle.pocket: THE HANDLE MAY REVERSE BEFORE THE DISTAL MASS IS ALLOWED TO.
principle.causal_thesis: A flexible distal mass is accelerated by a root-earned handle sweep. Contact interrupts the mass locally, but the body/handle begins braking and reversing before the distal mass has repaid its tangential momentum. The tether changes angle under this disagreement; the mass overshoots, crosses the handle's recovery line, then returns late while support catches residual torque. Recovery is therefore a two-clock debt repayment, not reverse interpolation.
principle.novelty_vs_canonical_003_014: Introduces flexible-tool phase disagreement: proximal handle/root reversal and distal mass reversal are authored as separate causal events. Unlike rigid-tool clearance, bind, glancing-axis, offhand-countertorque, body-clock fork, or limb-root overrun studies, the force-carrying endpoint remains dynamically late because custody is continuous through a flexible tether.

source.name: Billy & Jimmy
observed: Authoritative campaign evidence records the entire 829x786 PNG sheet as inspected.
Whole-sheet relationship evidence includes attacker-side Hair Grab / Knee Elbow / Kick / Shoulder Throw families and receiver-side Held / Punched / Grabbed / Kneed / Throw states.

The distal-mass-versus-handle reversal split is a transferable flexible-tool principle, not a claim about source choreography or game physics.

keys.name: OFFSET_READY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root is left/back of the target; distal mass hangs forward-low with a slack diagonal tether.
keys.causal_role: Asymmetric baseline: offhand is forward as counterweight while the handle hand owns the rear pocket.

keys.name: REAR_COIL
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Pelvis drops back/down while the handle hand retracts; distal mass remains forward, increasing tether angle.
keys.causal_role: Specific asymmetric load: root and handle move first while distal mass visibly resists the reversal.

keys.name: MASS_LATE_COIL
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Chest counterwinds above the loaded pelvis; handle rises but distal mass still trails low/right.
keys.causal_role: Makes proximal/distal phase separation readable before the strike begins.

keys.name: HANDLE_ACCELERATION
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root drives forward before the hand clears; chain bends behind the accelerating handle.
keys.causal_role: Pelvis/support earns the sweep; the distal mass still trails and cannot teleport to the attack line.

keys.name: PRECONTACT_ARC
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Lead support accepts weight; handle is already forward while mass climbs through a visible curved approach with target gap.
keys.causal_role: Distinct precontact: root/handle commitment precedes mass arrival; contact is not merely maximum reach.

keys.name: DISTAL_CONTACT
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root advances only one cell into the contact hold; handle remains inside the target line while distal mass meets the explicit contact point.
keys.causal_role: Explicit distal contact event with the chain still angled; the body has not exhausted its forward/root range.

keys.name: HANDLE_BRAKE_FIRST
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Lead support compresses and pelvis starts back while handle hand snaps one cell left; distal mass remains to the right.
keys.causal_role: The proximal clock reverses first. The distal endpoint is deliberately still late, exposing tether disagreement after impact.

keys.name: DISTAL_OVERSHOOT
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root retreats while the mass continues down/right; the tether steepens even though the handle is already recovering left.
keys.causal_role: Visible distal overshoot survives contact and handle reversal; recovery cannot be a mirrored rewind.

keys.name: TETHER_CROSSOVER
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root continues left/up; distal mass finally reverses and crosses below the handle recovery line.
keys.causal_role: Separate distal reversal event: tether angle changes sign after the handle/root have already reversed.

keys.name: MASS_RECOIL_LAG
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Pelvis nearly stabilizes while mass continues leftward under the hand and rear foot widens.
keys.causal_role: Secondary lag transfers from root to distal mass; the body is mostly caught while the flexible tool is not.

keys.name: SUPPORT_TORQUE_CATCH
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root counterleans into wide support while the returning mass rises behind the handle; offhand opens opposite the swing.
keys.causal_role: Support and offhand catch the tether's returning torque without stopping the distal clock instantly.

keys.name: SECONDARY_PENDULUM_SETTLE
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root holds its displaced address while the distal mass makes one smaller forward/down settle.
keys.causal_role: A reduced-amplitude pendulum settle pays residual flexible-tool debt after body stabilization.

keys.name: DISPLACED_REENTRY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Ready re-entry stays four cells forward of K00; mass hangs in a shorter rear/low pocket rather than returning to its initial location.
keys.causal_role: Recovery debt closes at a new address with a changed tether rest angle; no idle reset.
